risks: Minimal for patients; for staff, the risk is that feedback feels like surveillance and that ward data are misused. Night alerts may disturb patients in shared bays.
consent: Wards are the unit of randomisation and staff are the participants whose behaviour is observed. Individual consent for observation is impracticable without distorting behaviour; the ethics board will be asked for a waiver of individual consent under the Ottawa Statement for cluster trials, with staff informed through the staff council, posters and huddles and able to raise concerns.
data: Observers record staff group and float status, never names; badge data are used at ward level only under agreement JSC-2026-07; data are kept on the infection prevention team's restricted drive.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: float, agency and junior staff have least control over workload and may experience feedback as surveillance most. Acceptability and compliance are reported by staff group, and no individual or staff-group data are shared with managers.
effectiveness: The trial decides whether a hospital-wide licence is worth buying; a precise null result on the observed outcome is as useful to the board as a positive one.
efficiency: Uses installed badges and 400 donated observer-hours.
costs: Feedback licence for eight wards for six months, provided by the vendor at no charge for the trial, and observer travel.
grants: None needed; an infection prevention research award could fund video-based outcome assessment in a follow-on trial.
partnerships: Staff council and unions, the regional infection prevention network (observers), ward managers, and two patient representatives from the infection prevention patient panel.
rebPath: Full review by the hospital research ethics board as a cluster randomised trial with a waiver of individual staff consent, following ICH-GCP and the Ottawa Statement; registration in a public trial registry before randomisation.
limitations: Observer visibility remains; six months may be too short for durable change; infections are not an evaluable outcome.
summary: Cluster trial with a staff consent waiver request, ward-level data use only, and equity reporting by staff group.
